newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle launch gets green light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle launch gets green light.

text.p: Space shuttle Columbia was cleared for launch on Friday after engineers resolved a nagging booster rocket problem, U.S. space agency officials said on Monday.
Columbia was scheduled to blast off from Florida's Kennedy Space Centre on Friday at 2:50 p.m. EST (1950 GMT), one week later than originally planned.
The mission had been delayed so engineers could conclude an investigation into the perplexing rocket problem, which cropped up on the last shuttle flight.
"We now feel like we understand the booster problem," NASA spokesman Bruce Buckingham said at the conclusion of a flight readiness review by shuttle managers.

Space agency officials wanted to determine exactly what caused about 60 gouges in the protective insulation that lined the bell-like nozzle of a solid rocket booster used by shuttle Atlantis in September.
Columbia's crew of five was due to arrive at the Kennedy Space Centre from Houston on Monday evening.
During the 16-day mission the astronauts are due to release and later retrieve a pair of science satellites, and make two spacewalks to study space station construction techniques.
